title: Three leg days a week because I’m a busy dad and business owner, not because I have unlimited time.
hook: Three leg days a week because I’m a busy dad and business owner, not because I have unlimited time.
caption:
Three leg days a week because I’m a busy dad and business owner, not because I have unlimited time.

Splitting legs lets me hit every muscle group at least twice a week in shorter, more focused workouts while keeping weekly volume high enough to grow. I keep intensity up with drop sets, then recover and come back to each area with purpose.

Monday: glutes, lower back, hamstrings, calves
Wednesday: quads and calves
Friday: hamstrings, quads, calves, glutes

More frequent, efficient sessions. High volume. High intensity. Built around real life.

title: The scale going up does not automatically mean you gained fat.
hook: The scale going up does not automatically mean you gained fat.
caption:
The scale going up does not automatically mean you gained fat.

Your cycle, digestion, sodium, carbs, stress, sleep, and timing can all affect the number you see.

This is why I teach my clients to look at the full picture, not just one weigh-in.

Progress is not just the scale. It is your photos, measurements, strength, energy, clothes, and consistency.

Do not let one number make you quit.

title: Lifting heavy weight doesn't necessarily mean muscular growth.
hook: Lifting heavy weight doesn't necessarily mean muscular growth.
caption:
Lifting heavy weight doesn't necessarily mean muscular growth. 

Think again.

Muscles grow because of Hypertrophy.
Muscle hypertrophy is the body's adaptation to resistance training. In order to get bigger muscles much more is expected than just exhausting yourself in the gym.

The Hypertrophy fundamentals are simple to understand:
1. Mechanical tension
2. Progressive overload
3. Challenging sets
4. Adequate protein
5. Recovery & sleep
6. Consistency

It is necessary to give muscles a reason to adapt, recover and grow.
